title: Contract of a slice (protocol §6.1 in JSON): contract.json (S*) and the candidates contract_alpha.json / contract_beta.json of .a2dlc/run/<slice>/
description: Stage 1 produces it. In greenfield and brownfield_facade, Specifier α and β each write a candidate (source specifier_alpha / specifier_beta) and the Inquisitor merges them into S* (source consensus). In refactor the core derives it without LLM from the public signatures, with strict π_S: the legacy is the oracle. A subset of §6.1: functions with pre/post, errors and invariants in text, boundary probes, assumptions and π_S. Optional: io_contract, invariants (with the §6.2 DSL) and lemmas. Capabilities are declared in intent.capabilities. A probe is the concrete input and what S* says happens; probes.json blocks them with the hash of S*.

input_schema_ref.description: Reference to the input schema of the slice (a path in the repo or a URI).

output_schema_ref.description: Reference to the output schema of the slice.

error_taxonomy.description: Error codes the slice may raise. functions[].errors[].raises names, when present, must be among them.

invariants.description: Slice-level invariants. text is the statement; dsl is the invariant in the core's concrete syntax (protocol §6.2 names only a subset of it) that the core translates to SMT; verification says how it is checked.

name.description: In refactor, the target <file>::<symbol> of the signature; in greenfield, the name the specifier proposes.

signature.description: The header in the repo's language; null if the specifier does not fix it.

errors.description: Error taxonomy (§6.1 error_taxonomy) per function: under which condition and what it throws.

lemmas.description: Critical slices: pure internal functions with declared postconditions. The engine checks each one (crosshair per lemma; in refactor, diffbehavior against the base lemma of the same name).

smt.description: Block 7, optional. The pre/post of the function in SMT-LIB 2 (declare-const, define-fun, assert), for the satisfiability check of Stage 1.5 (§5: Z3 runs over these clauses; the §6.2 DSL of invariants[].dsl is translated by the core into this form). The z3 engine concatenates the fragments and solves them: unsat is CB-02a; unknown leaves the function as runtime_and_pbt. Absent: the function does not go through Z3 and the stage says so. Never Python code: only SMT-LIB, which the engine parses without evaluating.

probe.description: Boundary probe (§6.1 locked_boundary_probes): a concrete input and the result that S* fixes; with file and expr, also the assertion that Tier 0 runs. example: one case; property: a property over a family of inputs; negative: what must fail.

input.description: Expression or JSON, as a test would write it.

file.description: Optional, with expr: file of the candidate, relative to the repo, whose module Tier 0 imports to evaluate expr.

assumption.description: Optional: id of the S* assumption this probe checks (consensus probe, §5 Stage 1 step 4). Each catalogue assumption with status accepted requires at least one probe that cites it: agreement between families is not correctness. Validate requires the id to exist among the contract's assumptions.

expr.description: Optional, with file: the compiled assertion (protocol §5 Stage 1 step 5), a boolean expression in the engine's language evaluated with the module's top-level names in view; the Python engine adds raises(Exc, f, *args, **kwargs). A probe without expr is not run by Tier 0: it stays as unchecked in the candidate.

assumption.description: Domain assumption. source catalogue: comes from the catalogue (.a2dlc/catalogue.json) and its id is the entry's; specifier: an LLM proposed it and, until it enters the catalogue, it generates no probes (§5 Stage 1, opposite case). open waits for a person.

criticality.description: Block 7, optional. How costly it is to be wrong about the assumption. The Stage 1.5 lint gives an error for an open assumption of criticality high or critical: someone has to answer it before building. Absent: unknown, and an open assumption without criticality does not block.

pi_s.description: Equivalence relation π_S (§5 Stage 1.5 step 3): strict by default; each relaxation is explicit (ignored field, set semantics, tolerance, compare error_code) and is validated by a human probe.
